subject: Confidential: early correction check-in — Dylan Brooks
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Confidential: early correction check-in — Dylan Brooks

Hi Laura and Mina,

I wanted to start a short, confidential thread to document the coaching steps we've agreed to take with Dylan over the next 30 days. Over the past six weeks I've noted repeated missed checkpoints on the Q2 integration milestones and inconsistent handoffs to the infra team. I spoke briefly with Dylan yesterday to flag the pattern and set immediate expectations, but I'd like to formalize a short corrective plan and make sure HR is aware (confidentially) so we have a consistent record.

Proposed immediate steps: 
- 1:1 cadence: twice-weekly 30-min check-ins (Mon/Wed) for four weeks.
- Mutual action plan (MAP) with 3 concrete deliverables and acceptance criteria.
- Weekly deliverable tracker that Laura updates and I can view.
- Clear escalation point: if deliverable 1 is missed by more than 48 hours, we escalate to Mark (cc'd) to decide next steps.

Please find attached a draft matrix with the outstanding deliverables and examples (q2-deliverable-matrix.csv, examples-of-missing-deliverables.pdf). Mina, can you confirm any HR documentation templates we should use to keep this a pre-PIP coaching track? I'd prefer we preserve coaching / remediation language and avoid PIP wording unless we reach a trigger.

Dylan, the intent here is to be constructive and clear: we'll outline what success looks like for each deliverable and check in frequently. Expect a calendar invite from Laura to start the cadence if you're available.

Thanks,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Principal Product Manager, Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Confidential: early correction check-in — Dylan Brooks

Thanks Grace — I appreciate the framing. I've already had an informal sync with Dylan this morning; he acknowledged the missed checkpoints and asked for clearer acceptance criteria. I'm going to send a calendar invite for our twice-weekly check-ins starting Monday 10:00am PT and I'll populate the MAP with three deliverables:

1) Integration API contract sign-off — acceptance: merged PR + infra validation.
2) Data ingest script (+ unit tests) — acceptance: passing CI and demo run.
3) Handoff notes + runbook — acceptance: peer review and onboarding session scheduled.

I'll keep the tracker in the shared Drive link Grace included and update it after every check-in. If we see no measurable improvement after two weeks (i.e., missed acceptance on deliverable 1 & 2), then we should bring Mark in for a quick escalation meeting.

Attaching the coaching checklist template I usually use — it keeps tone corrective and not punitive.

Laura

[attachment: coaching-checklist-template.docx]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Confidential: early correction check-in — Dylan Brooks

Thanks, Laura and Grace. I want to acknowledge the misses — especially on the integration API contract where I underestimated the infra dependency. I appreciate the clear acceptance criteria; that helps.

A couple quick asks from my side: 
- Can we lock down which infra engineer is the contact for validation? last-minute changes were part of the delay.
- For the data ingest script, can I get an extra day for test coverage given the flaky staging environment?

I'll come to the first check-in with a draft timeline for each deliverable and blockers listed. I'm committed to hitting the criteria, and I welcome the support.

Dylan

Thank you for looping People Ops in, Grace and Laura. A few HR notes to keep this strictly as coaching and pre-PIP: 
- Use supportive language in all written updates ("action plan", "checkpoints", "expected outcomes") and avoid formal "PIP" terminology unless we cross triggers.
- Document each 1:1 with a short note (date, outcome, owner). Store notes in the shared Drive folder and mark access as private to the manager/HR/leadership as needed.
- I am attaching a redacted coaching checklist and an acknowledgement template for Dylan to sign that confirms he understands expectations and the cadence.

If deliverable acceptance criteria are explicit and measured (OKRs or binary pass/fail), it helps us objectively determine next steps. If you want, I'm available to join the first or second check-in to ensure documentation is complete.

Mina
People Partner, Talent Operations
Redwood Inference

[attachment: coaching-checklist-template.docx] [attachment: acknowledgement-template.docx]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Confidential: early correction check-in — Dylan Brooks

Appreciate the quick responses. Laura — thank you for taking point on the MAP and calendar invites. Dylan — locking an infra contact makes sense; I've asked Sergio in infra to be available for validation next week (I will confirm separately).

Next immediate actions (owner):
- Laura: send calendar invites + populate MAP in Drive (by EOD today).
- Dylan: upload draft timelines and blockers to Drive before Monday.
- Mina: if you can review our first two check-in notes and provide the acknowledgement template, that would be great.

We'll treat this as a documented coaching track. If by the second week there is no measurable progress on the first two deliverables, we'll convene Mark for a short calibration and determine whether this remains coaching or moves to formal PIP steps.

Thanks all — keeping this confidential and constructive.

Grace
Principal Product Manager, Inference
Redwood Inference
